Simulation-based exploration approach:

Some quotes from:

- Andrew Gelman
- Bret Victor
- Richard Feyman

Baking in solution is risky. It can payoff big time (the only way to learn
programming and algorithmic thinking is to study other people's code), but it
can also backfire (blind copy-pasting).

The statistics and concepts might be very simple but this is an advantage --
newbies learn about new statistics and their features, experts can use
simulations to dig even deeper.

Even people who did the short crashcourse will learn enough (three hours of
rushing was a bad idea and I stopped teaching that short tutorial completely
even at UCPH).


There's a lot of text. If you struggle with too much text on the screen, the **bold text** always indicates a concrete, actionable task to do in a given exercise.
